problem: LRM-based navigation agents either think at every step (dense thinking), which is costly and causes overthinking that hurts success, or use rule-based schedules (every-K-steps, action-only inference) that ignore navigation dynamics. No agent adaptively decides when to reason.
motivation: Long-horizon, real-time navigation needs low latency, and most steps (moving straight between trivial waypoints) need no deliberation. The authors observe that only ~30% of actions have high entropy, that these occur at novel scenes or critical objects, and that thinking only there gives the best Q-value/token-efficiency trade-off.
key_idea: Use the agent's own first-token action entropy to trigger chain-of-thought reasoning only for high-entropy actions (entropy above threshold 0.6), trained via hybrid SFT plus two-stage online RL.
insight: Entropy is a usable signal for when reasoning helps: thinking at low thresholds causes overthinking and at high thresholds causes underthinking (Q-value vs threshold, peak at 0.6). Dense thinking is far worse than no thinking (34.5 vs 70.0 SR after RL), so reasoning only helps when placed well. Directly RL-training hybrid mode collapses the no-thinking ability (3.5% drop), while two-stage RL with KL regularization avoids it. The No-Thinking Window is essential: with NTW=0 the agent falls into an 'entropy trap' of repeated high-entropy actions and fails to beat no-thinking.
method: Action entropy analysis: first-token entropy of the predicted action; ~30% of actions exceed 0.6, and these coincide with turns into new areas or near target objects. Mean-token entropy performs similarly (Table in appendix).
Hybrid reasoning strategy: predict the action in no-thinking mode first; if entropy exceeds tau=0.6, re-prompt in thinking mode and regenerate the action with CoT.
No-Thinking Window (NTW): thinking is allowed only every K=5 steps to prevent repeated high-entropy triggering (overthinking loops).

Hybrid Reasoning Dataset + H-SFT: 2.86M expert (observation, action) pairs from a PoliFormer RL policy form the no-reasoning data. The top 20% highest-entropy samples get Gemini-2.0-Flash CoT traces (bootstrapped until they match the GT action, then filtered), giving 280K reasoning pairs. Qwen2.5-VL-3B is fine-tuned on both with a mode prompt.
Annotated semantic map (ASM) memory: a top-down map with explored area, trajectory, and landmark object annotations serves as long-term memory, alongside a 4-frame short-term window.

Two-stage online PPO: Stage I rolls out in no-thinking mode and trains only no-thinking ability. Stage II rolls out with the hybrid strategy, applies the PPO loss only to thinking-mode samples, and adds a KL penalty (beta=0.1) to the Stage-I model on no-thinking samples. Trained on ProcTHOR-150k with the PoliFormer reward, using Verl-Agent.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-3B (H-SFT then PPO, fine-tuned LLM params only)
setting.training_data: 2.86M expert pairs from a PoliFormer policy (no-reasoning dataset); 280K Gemini-2.0-Flash reasoning traces on top-20% high-entropy samples; online PPO on ProcTHOR-150k houses with Objaverse assets
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (4-frame short-term window) + annotated semantic map as long-term memory (built from GT object locations and simulator depth)
setting.action_space: low-level textual actions: move_ahead 0.2 m, move_back 0.2 m, rotate left/right 30°, rotate left/right small 5°, end
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (CHORES-S ObjectNav, SPOC/PoliFormer setup, Stretch RE-1)
setting.privileged: ASM built from ground-truth object locations and simulator depth in the main results (replaced by Depth-Anything + Mask R-CNN in a robustness test)

numbers_note: Only one benchmark (CHORES-S ObjectNav, 200 tasks); split not explicitly named, so 'test' is assumed. Pass@k results (95.5% GT, 92.0% DM at k=16) are given in a figure and text only.
results: HiRO-Nav with hybrid reasoning gets 81.0 SR / 57.2 SEL using ~2.7e3 tokens per episode. It beats thinking-every-K-steps (78.5 SR, 3.5e3 tokens), no-thinking (70.0), dense-thinking (34.5, 3.1e4 tokens), and o3/Gemini2.5-Pro dense-thinking (27.0/27.5 SR). It stays robust with noisy ASMs (72.0 SR), and Pass@16 reaches 95.5%.
limitations: Relies on a hand-set entropy threshold and a reactive design that first predicts an action and then regenerates it with CoT, adding latency.
Only evaluated on simulated CHORES-S ObjectNav with GT object/depth-based semantic maps; no real robot and no other benchmarks.
Needs the NTW heuristic to avoid the entropy trap, and a costly pipeline (PoliFormer expert data, Gemini annotation, two-stage RL).
